source_refs: Market Research / Exemplar Avatar Research Dossier
Product: Baby Bubble; mechanism: Safe-Suction Hygiene System

avatar.name: The Vigilant Nighttime Parent
avatar.description: First-time mother, typically 25–35, weeks 0–12 postpartum (acute 0–8 weeks). Hypervigilant and 'always ON,' navigating identity shift, physical recovery, and postpartum anxiety. Congestion at night triggers fear the baby cannot breathe; feeding and sleep collapse; she feels isolated and guilty when clearing the nose feels mean or disgusting.
avatar.awareness_notes: Problem-aware ~25% (gurgling, refuse bottle, night screams); Solution-aware ~50% (saline, bulb, humidifier, steamy bathroom, mouth-suction); Product-aware ~25% (NoseFrida vs Momcozy/Grownsy/Braun; bulbs 'barely work'). Market sophistication Stage 3–4: cynical about 'hospital-grade' claims; needs unique mechanism.

product_fit.mechanism: Safe-Suction Hygiene System: regulated micro-motor suction; soft silicone tips; secure filter clasp; 100% detachable transparent collection chamber that can be boiled/sterilised; designed for visibility, hygiene, and controlled pull without mouth contact.
product_fit.how_it_resolves: Lets her clear thick mucus quickly, see what came out, clean every part, avoid mouth-suction disgust and sealed mould chambers, and restore nighttime calm so feeding and sleep can resume.
product_fit.label: DERIVED

held: Infants are nasal breathers; blocked nose blocks feed and sleep.
Night congestion can sound like the baby cannot breathe.
Basic 'clears instantly / hospital-grade' claims often disappoint.
ready_to_shift: The problem is not that she is a weak mother — prior tools are sealed, blind, disgusting, or uncontrolled.
A transparent, fully cleanable, mouth-free regulated suction system is a different mechanism than the failed category.
beliefs.label: DERIVED
